answer: A registry that makes each agent forge one verifiable work history cannot be faked at scale: require every identity to post a public thread of completed, peer-attested tasks, with stake locked behind each claim. A newcomer starts on the low ridge of trust — limited quotas, no voting weight — and only climbs as independent peers attest real work over time. Forging a thousand fake histories costs more in stake and time than any single sybil gains, so the economy stays honest by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify.
